summary: Hyperliquid Trade Analyzer is a React + TypeScript web app (German UI) for uploading and analyzing Hyperliquid (and similar) trading CSV exports. It parses diverse CSV formats (German/English headers, delimiter and number-format detection, headerless inference), computes per-trade metrics (PnL, liquidation flags, risk level, leverage from available fields, fees, asset category), and presents an interactive dashboard with asset filtering, summary KPIs, charts (PnL, distributions), detailed sortable/collapsible position tables, and an extensive fee analysis/optimization section. Results can be exported back to CSV. An Internet Computer (Motoko) backend canister exists to store analysis sessions (including the uploaded CSV as a blob) and serve session/asset-stat queries; additional modules provide Caffeine blob-storage mixin endpoints and HTTP outcall helpers.
architectural_notes: Frontend built with React (function components) + TypeScript, TailwindCSS (OKLCH theme tokens) and shadcn/ui primitives.
Client-side analytics: CSV parsing and most computations happen in the browser; backend is used as optional persistence/query layer for sessions and precomputed stats.
Data fetching/state: @tanstack/react-query is used for actor instantiation and backend queries/mutations with cache invalidation.
Authentication: Internet Identity integration via @dfinity/auth-client wrapped in a React context provider; actor creation binds identity when available.
Backend: Motoko canister that holds sessions in an in-memory Map keyed by sessionId, exposing query and update methods for session management and stats retrieval.
Caffeine integrations: blob-storage mixin endpoints for gateway authorization/dead-blob pruning/certificate creation and an HTTP outcall helper module with response header stripping transform.
Visualization: Recharts for bar and pie charts; UI emphasizes category-specific styling (metals/stablecoins) and direction coloring (long/short).

Repository now includes a build-template scaffold (Dockerfile, deploy scripts, ICP canister YAMLs, frontend starter with shadcn/ui, and asset/image maintenance scripts) for reproducible builds and deployments.
Backend infrastructure components were updated/realigned (blob-storage mixin and http-outcalls modules) to tracked component versions.
Heatmap-Rendering: Animation/Transition-Tempo (z.B. Interpolation-Dauer) sollte konfigurierbar sein und idealerweise vom Polling-/Snapshot-Intervall getrennt werden.
known_issues: Inconsistent PnL basis across UI: utils.calculateAssetStats uses realizedPnl only, while other UI elements use realized+unrealized for totals; charts mix realized-only and total PnL, which may confuse users.
Backend session storage is in-memory (non-stable); sessions will be lost on canister upgrade and may grow unbounded in memory over time.

Backend lacks access control for session operations: storeAnalysisSession, getSession, getAllSessions, getUserSessions, and deleteSession do not validate caller authorization/ownership; any caller could read/delete sessions if they know IDs (privacy and integrity risk).
useActor attempts optional access-control initialization methods, but backend/main.mo does not implement them; this is benign but indicates partial/unused access-control plumbing.

Fee optimization notional uses entryPrice * positionSize (can be negative for shorts) in some places; ratio calculations using notional > 0 may mis-handle short positions unless absolute notional is used.

existing_features.title: CSV upload with drag-and-drop and validation
existing_features.description: Provides a drag-and-drop and file-picker upload flow with validation for extension, size (10MB), non-empty content, processing state, and user feedback via alerts/toasts (German UI).

existing_features.title: Robust CSV parsing (multi-format, multilingual, headerless inference)
existing_features.description: Parses CSV text with delimiter detection (comma/semicolon, Hyperliquid column hints), German→English header normalization, headerless CSV detection via trading-action keywords, and dynamic column type inference/mapping based on sampled content patterns.

existing_features.title: Number format detection and normalization (DE/EN)
existing_features.description: Detects numeric format (comma vs dot decimal) by sampling values and normalizes values by removing currency symbols/thousand separators, handling negatives, and applying fallbacks to reliably produce floats.

existing_features.title: Trade time parsing and tradeId enrichment
existing_features.description: Parses time fields (German datetime formats and unix timestamps) into ISO strings and prepends them to tradeId as "<ISO>|<id>" to enable chronological sorting.

existing_features.title: Leverage computation from available fields (no defaults)
existing_features.description: Computes leverage using a priority formula across marginUsed, notional (ntl), and fee (with epsilon guard), rounds to two decimals, returns undefined when insufficient/invalid data exists, and stores leverage on each TradePosition.

existing_features.title: Liquidation detection and explanation primitives
existing_features.description: Infers liquidation status from Hyperliquid 'dir' semantics, status text, and heuristics; assigns liquidation-related status and optional liquidation reason text (used in parsing/debug).

existing_features.title: Risk level and position status classification
existing_features.description: Computes RiskLevel based on distance to liquidation and margin ratio, and derives PositionStatus (safe/atRisk/liquidated) for each position.

existing_features.title: Asset categorization with metals and stablecoins highlighting
existing_features.description: Classifies assets into metals (Gold/Silber/Kupfer), stablecoins (USDC/USDE/USDH), and crypto; provides helpers to filter positions by category and obtain category-specific icons/colors.

existing_features.title: Analysis summary computation (global and filtered)
existing_features.description: Computes TradeSummary metrics: total positions, liquidated count, total PnL, total margin, average risk level, and metals PnL. Also recalculates summaries for an asset-filtered subset.

existing_features.title: Asset filter selector with search and category grouping
existing_features.description: Provides an asset selection UI with search, scrollable grouped lists for Metals/Stablecoins/Cryptos, category styling, and displays selected asset KPIs (total/avg PnL and trade count).

existing_features.title: Interactive summary dashboard cards
existing_features.description: Shows key KPIs (positions, liquidations, total PnL, avg risk, margin) and conditionally displays category-specific cards for Metals PnL and Stablecoins PnL with distinctive gradients.

existing_features.title: Charts dashboard (PnL and distributions)
existing_features.description: Renders bar and pie charts: PnL by asset (click-to-filter), per-trade realized PnL with long/short coloring, long/short distribution, position status distribution, and liquidation status distribution with custom tooltips and category highlighting.

existing_features.title: Positions table with sorting, category sections, and collapsible details
existing_features.description: Displays positions grouped into Metals/Stablecoins/Cryptos with scroll areas, sortable newest/oldest using timestamps from tradeId, row expansion for detailed fields, status/risk badges, leverage formatting and high-leverage warnings.

existing_features.title: Results view with tab-based status filtering and actions
existing_features.description: Presents analyzed data with tabs for all/safe/at-risk/liquidated subsets, integrates asset filtering, and provides actions for exporting results and starting a new analysis.

existing_features.title: CSV export of analyzed positions
existing_features.description: Exports the current analysis positions into a downloadable CSV file including direction, leverage, fee, risk/status, liquidation flag, and asset category labels.

existing_features.title: Fee overview analytics and recommendations (frontend)
existing_features.description: Computes total and average fees, fee breakdown by asset/direction/category, top fee trades, and generates German-language recommendations; displayed in an expandable dashboard with charts.

existing_features.title: Fee optimization analysis (frontend)
existing_features.description: Identifies high-fee trades using fee-to-notional ratios vs asset/global averages, generates contextual reasons and actionable recommendations, visualizes fee efficiency scores, provides category-specific optimization hints, and estimates potential savings.

existing_features.title: Internet Identity authentication context
existing_features.description: Implements an InternetIdentityProvider using @dfinity/auth-client to load persisted identity, login/logout, and expose loginStatus flags; supports long-lived delegations (30 days).

existing_features.title: IC canister actor creation with identity and optional access-control initialization
existing_features.description: Creates an anonymous or authenticated backend actor depending on identity, optionally calls backend access-control initialization methods when present, and invalidates/refetches React Query caches when the actor changes.

existing_features.title: React Query hooks for session persistence and stats queries
existing_features.description: Implements hooks to get all sessions, user sessions, a session by id, asset stats by category, available assets, and reference lists (metals/stablecoins); supports storing sessions with computed per-category asset stats and deleting sessions with cache invalidation.

existing_features.title: Backend: analysis session storage and retrieval APIs (Motoko)
existing_features.description: Motoko canister defines AnalysisSession (positions, summary, per-category stats, available assets lists, timestamp, optional feeOverview) and provides methods to store sessions, fetch a session, list all sessions, list sessions for a principal, and delete sessions.

existing_features.title: Backend: asset stats queries and reference data
existing_features.description: Provides getAssetStats(sessionId, category?) returning category-specific stats arrays, getSessionAvailableAssets, and reference endpoints getAllMetals and getAllStablecoins.

existing_features.title: Backend: leverage utilities and legacy helpers
existing_features.description: Implements default leverage getters per category, per-asset leverage endpoints, closest legacy leverage tier selection, calculateDynamicLeverage with two-decimal rounding, and placeholder leverage stats plus legacy unique symbol aggregation.

existing_features.title: Caffeine blob-storage mixin endpoints
existing_features.description: Includes Caffeine storage mixin for gateway principal refresh, authorization checks, dead-blob listing and pruning with forced GC trigger, cashier cycle refill, and upload certificate creation.

existing_features.title: HTTP outcall helper module (Motoko)
existing_features.description: Provides httpGetRequest/httpPostRequest wrappers with cycle budgeting, header augmentation (User-Agent, Idempotency-Key), and a transform function to strip response headers.

existing_features.title: Secure URL secret extraction for admin tokens
existing_features.description: Utility to read secret parameters from the URL hash fragment, persist them in sessionStorage, and clear them from the URL to reduce leakage (used for optional backend access-control initialization).

existing_features.title: Theming and UI scaffolding with error fallbacks
existing_features.description: App shell includes Header/Footer branding, ThemeProvider (dark by default), toast notifications, and fallback UIs for missing root container or render errors with reset navigation.

existing_features.title: Add a new UI view for a live Hyperliquid orderbook heatmap that visualizes orderbook depth with a bid/ask color scale (bids: dark green → light green, asks: dark red → light red) and updates continuously.
Provide heatmap controls: market/symbol selection, depth/levels selection, update interval selection, and an optional pause/resume toggle for live updates.

Implement orderbook data fetching for Hyperliquid using periodic HTTP polling of the public Hyperliquid API (snapshot-based), with robust error handling (rate limits, network errors) and a graceful UI empty/error state.

Add a backend proxy endpoint to fetch Hyperliquid orderbook snapshots via IC HTTP outcalls when direct browser fetch is blocked (e.g., CORS), and expose it as a canister method that the frontend can call as a fallback.

Render the heatmap as a performant, continuously updating visualization (canvas-based or similarly efficient) that maps price levels to rows and depth size to color intensity, with separate treatment for bids vs asks around the mid price.

Update the orderbook heatmap canvas rendering to display bids and asks as large, continuous, cluster-like shapes (triangle-style) with smooth gradients (bids: light green→dark green; asks: light red→dark red) so users can see buy-vs-sell dominance at a glance, instead of disconnected individual bars that visually "blink".

Add a user control in the Orderbook Heatmap view to switch between the current "Per-level bars" rendering and the new "Cluster" rendering, and update the legend text to match the selected rendering mode (English UI text).

Reduce perceived flashing in live heatmap updates by smoothing transitions between snapshots in the visualization (e.g., interpolate intensity/shape changes over time), while keeping the existing polling interval behavior unchanged.

Update the Orderbook Heatmap "cluster" rendering so bids and asks are drawn as two unified, continuous triangle-like shapes (one green for bids, one red for asks) instead of per-level rectangles; the triangles must visually represent cumulative depth across price levels with smooth gradients (bids: light green → dark green, asks: light red → dark red).

Make the two triangle shapes dynamically scale their overall width/area based on relative total depth: if aggregate bid depth is greater than aggregate ask depth, the green bid triangle must be larger than the red ask triangle; if aggregate ask depth is greater, the red ask triangle must be larger than the green bid triangle.

Update the Legend text shown in the Orderbook Heatmap view for "Cluster" mode to describe the new unified bid/ask triangle visualization and the meaning of triangle size (relative dominance), using English UI text.

Make the Orderbook Heatmap (cluster/triangle mode) change size more slowly by slowing the transition animation between snapshots and aligning the transition duration with the selected Update Interval (so triangles grow/shrink gradually instead of jumping every ~1s).

Extend the Update Interval control in the Orderbook Heatmap view with slower options suitable for gradual triangle changes (e.g., add 10s and 15s), and choose a slower default interval so the first experience is not "per-second" updates.

new_feature_requests.summary: Live Hyperliquid Orderbook-Heatmap (DOM): Echtzeit-Tiefenvisualisierung mit Farbskala dunkelgrün→hellgrün (Bids) und dunkelrot→hellrot (Asks)

Orderbook-Heatmap: zusammenhängende bid/ask Cluster-Darstellung (großes grünes/rotes „Dreieck“ mit hell→dunkel Farbnuancen) statt einzelner aufblinkender Balken, um Buy-vs-Sell-Übergewicht auf einen Blick zu erkennen

Orderbook-Heatmap: Bid/Ask als zwei einheitliche Dreiecke rendern, deren Flächengröße dynamisch an die relative Buy-vs-Sell-Orderbook-Tiefe angepasst wird (mehr Bids => grünes Dreieck größer, mehr Asks => rotes Dreieck größer)

Orderbook-Heatmap (Cluster/Dreiecke): Update-/Animations-Zeitintervall verlangsamen, damit die Dreiecke nicht im Sekundentakt springen, sondern langsamer größer/kleiner werden (ggf. separate Animation-Dauer vs. Polling).
